system.name: PICACHU
system.one_liner: a plug-in coarse-grained reconfigurable accelerator (CGRA) that offloads nonlinear operations in LLM inference

components.name: ML Models
components.role: input models (e.g. PyTorch/ONNX) fed into the compiler

components.name: Translating to MLIR
components.role: lowers the input model into MLIR Linalg/Affine dialects

components.name: Pattern Matching
components.role: identifies nonlinear-operation patterns (e.g. GELU) in the MLIR and marks them for CGRA offload

components.name: Offloading
components.role: converts matched patterns into CGRA function calls in FP or INT versions

components.name: Lowering to LLVM IR
components.role: lowers the offloaded CGRA calls into LLVM IR using predefined kernel code

components.name: Loop Transformation
components.role: unrolls and vectorizes the kernel loops

components.name: DFG Manipulation
components.role: generates, tunes and maps the dataflow graph for the CGRA

components.name: DFG Generation
components.role: builds one DFG node per LLVM IR instruction, converting control flow to data flow

components.name: DFG Tuning
components.role: fuses common instruction patterns into single DFG nodes

components.name: DFG Mapping
components.role: maps the DFG onto the CGRA's Modulo Routing Resource Graph across cycles

components.name: Evaluation
components.role: uses an RTL framework to measure power, area, and other metrics

content.key_idea: PICACHU's compiler lowers models to MLIR, pattern-matches nonlinear operations for CGRA offload, then progressively transforms the resulting kernel into a tuned, cycle-mapped dataflow graph for RTL evaluation.
content.reading_order: Left to right along the top row of five pipeline-stage boxes, then down into each stage's code/IR snippet, and into the Loop Transformation / DFG Manipulation detail below.

summary: This figure lays out PICACHU's compiler toolchain as a five-stage pipeline: ML Models are translated to MLIR in the Linalg/Affine dialects, Pattern Matching locates nonlinear-operation patterns (illustrated with a GeLU example split into its five constituent instructions), Offloading converts matches into CGRA function calls in FP or INT versions, and the result is Lowered to LLVM IR using predefined kernel code. Each stage box is paired with a concrete code or IR snippet showing exactly what it does to the running example. Below the main pipeline, a Loop Transformation stage unrolls and vectorizes the kernel, and a DFG Manipulation stage generates, tunes (fusing common instruction patterns) and cycle-maps the dataflow graph onto the CGRA's routing resource graph, feeding an Evaluation stage that reports power, area and other metrics via an RTL framework.
summary_zh: 该图展示 PICACHU 编译器五阶段流水线：模型转为 MLIR，匹配非线性算子（如 GELU）后卸载为 FP/INT 版 CGRA 调用并降为 LLVM IR；下方做循环展开/向量化与 DFG 生成、调优、映射，最终评估功耗与面积。
